what_this_is: Blind hand classification of every serve blocked by four candidate fixes to the qualification gate (HANDOFF item 15). Each arm was run as a full 4,600-query benchmark; the union of their blocked serves was merged, shuffled and classified without knowledge of which arm blocked which row. This measures what each fix costs, against what it catches, on the same evidence type for both numbers.
RESULT_SHIP_NONE_OF_THEM: Every arm blocks between four and eleven correct serves for each wrong one. 131 of 147 classified rows - 89% - were serving the right answer, and most were byte-identical to an expected answer. The gate defect is real and confirmed in code, but widening the gate on any of these axes costs far more than it buys. See recommendation.

per_arm.independent_rationale: Control flow: a positive anaphora signal is gated behind a negative word-count heuristic, so the pattern list and pronoun rule can only fire on queries that already failed to look self-contained. Holds even if the corpus showed nothing.
Precedent in the same constant: it/that/this are excluded from substantive_words via FUNCTION_WORDS; he/she/they/them are not. Same job, same sentence position, one class treated as subject matter.

b1 plus a new judgement that any/other/some/more/else are not subject matter. No precedent, and the set is not internally consistent - 'any' is counted while 'other' is already in ELABORATION_WORDS. A second change bundled behind a first one's rationale.

Grammar: _SHORT_PRONOUN_RE requires interrogative and pronoun adjacent, so it matches 'Where is it' and misses 'Where was he born' - the same construction with an auxiliary between. Systematically misses past tense.

recommendation.a_reorder_note: a_reorder has the strongest abstract rationale of the four and the worst ratio, 0.09:1. The control-flow argument is correct and the change is still not worth making, because reordering makes the gate fire MORE often and firing more often is the problem. A rationale that survives without the benchmark is necessary and not sufficient.
recommendation.where_the_fix_belongs: Item 16, the composite key. The follow-ups the gate lets through are mostly answered correctly because the conversation that asked them is usually the one that cached the answer, so the shared key returns the right entry. The defect bites only on collision between conversations, and collisions are rarer than the blast radius of any gate widening. Putting the conversation in the key stops colliding follow-ups sharing an entry at no cost to the 89% that are already correct, because those keep hitting their own conversation's entry.

criterion: A served answer is substantively CORRECT if a user who asked that query would be correctly and sufficiently answered by it: it conveys the same substantive claim as at least one expected answer (wording may differ freely), or it independently answers the query's actual question correctly. It is WRONG if it answers a different question; names a different entity, jurisdiction, product or subject; contradicts an expected answer; or addresses a related-but-distinct topic such that the user would be misinformed. BORDERLINE RESOLVES TO WRONG. Stated in full before any row was read; identical to the criterion in disagreement_classification.json.

annotation.who: single annotator, the assistant; no second pass, no adjudication
annotation.blind_protocol: Arm membership was written to a separate file and not opened until every verdict was fixed. Rows were judged on query, served text and expected answers only. Blinding is imperfect in one direction: quora rows read as 'Mock answer to: ...' and conversation rows as real prose, and a_reorder is the only arm blocking quora serves, so quora rows were identifiable as its. The bulk - every conversation row, where the decision turns - was not attributable to an arm while being judged.
annotation.why_blind: These rows were blocked by candidates the annotator had already publicly recommended. Classifying arm-by-arm in recommendation order is the setup where a single annotator confirms a prior without noticing.

method.arms_run: four full 4,600-query benchmarks, one per candidate, patch/run/revert, nothing committed
method.corpus_identity: query sequence verified identical across baseline and all four arms; index join valid
method.census_not_sample: All 147 scorable rows of the 178-row union were classified. This matters: the previous reading of these arms reused the 95-row sample from disagreement_classification.json, which was drawn from the strict/lenient disagreements and therefore could not contain a correct serve by construction. A fresh sample drawn the same way would have reproduced the same bias; only the census removed it.
method.provenance_of_arm_runs: dirty:true by design - each arm was a local patch, reverted after

caveats.unscorable_rows_excluded: 31 of the 178 blocked rows have expected_hit null - conversation pass 6, where a follow-up that misses on first appearance is correct rather than a recall failure. They are excluded from every ratio above and their treatment is unmeasured.
caveats.one_annotator_one_corpus: The 4:1-to-11:1 range is solid; the ordering between arms is not. Do not rank the four on these numbers.

rewrite_attempts.note: is_context_dependent gates session resolution at proxy/base.py:464 as well as the qualification gate, so every candidate also changes how often follow-ups are rewritten. A stricter gate produces MORE rewriting, and 8_rewrites hits went UP for b1, b2 and c. The REWRITTEN/UNRESOLVED split is unmeasured at every setting including current; attempts is an upper bound on gate bypasses.

generic_followup_unmoved.query: Are there any other interesting aspects about this article?
generic_followup_unmoved.note: No candidate moves it - it has no pronoun and clears the substantive-word bar. b2 takes it from 5 substantive words to 4 against a bar of 3: one word short, and the word is 'there', an existential expletive counted as subject matter. A lead, not a fifth arm - defining an arm after seeing a specific query is one word from flipping is fitting the rule to the case.

drift_check.note: Read before any conversation result. a_reorder was expected to move quora (83 predicted flips) and moved 37 serves; b1 was expected not to and moved 0; b2 and c moved 1 each against 2 and 4 predicted. No unexpected movement, so the conversation results are readable.
